373: \section{The Hopf Algebra of symmetric functions}\label{sec:Hopf}
374: Fix a valid tuple $\varphi=(n,r,i,j,a,b,N)$. View the linear forms $\linear_{\varphi}(\nu)$ as vectors in the ambient vector space $V$ with basis
375: $\left\{A_{\lambda,\theta} \right\}_{\lambda,\theta}$, where $\lambda,\theta\subseteq (n-r)^r$.
376: Let $T$ be the linear isomorphism $T:V\to \overline{\Lambda}\otimes \overline{\Lambda}$ defined by
377: \[T(A_{\lambda,\theta}) = \overline{s}_{\lambda}\otimes \overline{s}_{\theta}.\]
378: We use this isomorphism to give a useful perspective on the vectors $\linear_{\varphi}(\nu)\in V$ via
379: the (ring) product structure on $\overline{\Lambda}\otimes\overline{\Lambda}$ and
380: the coproduct map
381: \[\Delta:\Lambda\to \Lambda\otimes\Lambda.\]
382: Recall the coproduct $\Delta$ on symmetric functions acts on Schur functions by
383: \[\Delta(s_{\nu}) = \sum_{\lambda,\mu} c_{\lambda,\mu}^\nu (s_\lambda\otimes s_{\mu}).\]
384: Since the projection $\Lambda\to\overline{\Lambda}$ naturally induces a projection
385: \[\Lambda\otimes \Lambda \to \overline{\Lambda}\otimes \overline{\Lambda}, \]
386: we will also denote the latter with overlines.
387: \begin{definition}
388: \label{def:cp}
389: We define a linear endomorphism $\mathrm{CP}:\overline{\Lambda}\otimes \overline{\Lambda}\to \overline{\Lambda}\otimes \overline{\Lambda}$ as follows.
390: For a simple tensor $\overline{s}_\lambda\otimes \overline{s}_\mu\in \overline{\Lambda}\otimes\overline{\Lambda}$, define
391: \begin{align}
392: \mathrm{CP}(\overline{s}_\lambda\otimes \overline{s}_\mu) = \begin{cases}
393: \overline{\Delta(s_{\lambda})} - (\overline{s}_{\lambda}\otimes 1) &\mbox{ if $\overline{s}_\mu= 1$},\\
394: \overline{\Delta(s_{\lambda})}(1\otimes \overline{s}_{\mu}) &\mbox{ if $\overline{s}_\mu\neq 1$}.
395: \end{cases}
396: \end{align}
397: Define $\mathrm{CP}$ on all of $\overline{\Lambda}\otimes \overline{\Lambda}$ by extending linearly.
